This is a genuine bug, not expected behavior. The root cause is in `_coord_matrix` (astropy/modeling/separable.py:171-216), which builds the per-model coordinate matrix used by `_cstack` for the `&` operator.

When a child of `&` is itself a CompoundModel (e.g. `cm = Linear1D(10) & Linear1D(5)`), `_coord_matrix` does not recurse into it. Instead it only checks `model.separable` (line 202). For a separable compound model it falls into the `else` branch (lines 209-215), which builds a diagonal matrix `mat[i, i] = 1` for `i in range(model.n_inputs)` and, for a right child, rolls it by `noutp - model.n_outputs`. That diagonal construction assumes the child's outputs map one-to-one onto its own inputs in order, which is wrong for a nested compound whose internal structure is not a simple identity-like diagonal. The result is that the nested `cm` contributes a full 2x2 block of True values instead of the correct diagonal, producing the observed `[[T,T,F,F],[T,T,F,F],[F,F,T,T],[F,F,T,T]]`.

By contrast, the flat case `Pix2Sky_TAN() & Linear1D(10) & Linear1D(5)` works because each `&` operand is a simple (non-compound) model, so `_coord_matrix`'s diagonal path is correct for each leaf.

The fix would be to make `_coord_matrix` recurse into compound models (calling `_separable`/`_cstack` on the nested model) rather than treating any separable model as a diagonal. I did not read the full `_separable` dispatch (lines 271-313) or `_cdot`, so I cannot rule out related issues for `|` with nested compounds; that remains uncertain.

The user's report is a misunderstanding of the output, not a bug in the algorithm. In sqf_list, the second element of each (factor, multiplicity) pair is the multiplicity, and the factors are grouped by multiplicity. For (x**2+1)*(x-1)**2*(x-2)**3*(x-3)**3 the correct square-free decomposition is indeed (1, [(x**2+1, 1), (x-1, 2), (x-2, 3), (x-3, 3)]): the two distinct cubic-multiplicity factors (x-2) and (x-3) each have multiplicity 3, so they appear as two separate entries both with exponent 3. They are NOT combined into (x**2-5x+6, 3) because square-free factorization returns irreducible-ish square-free factors, not products of distinct factors sharing a multiplicity. The second example, x**5-2x**4-2x**3+4x**2+x-2 = (x-2)(x**2-1)**2, correctly yields (1, [(x-2, 1), (x**2-1, 2)]) because x**2-1 is itself square-free (it factors as (x-1)(x+1), both multiplicity 2, but sqf_list over ZZ does not split it further since x**2-1 is square-free). So both outputs are consistent with the documented semantics.

Evidence: dup_sqf_list (sympy/polys/sqfreetools.py:281-335) builds result by appending (g, i) for each multiplicity i, so distinct factors with the same multiplicity i are appended as separate tuples with the same exponent. Poly.sqf_list (sympy/polys/polytools.py:3210-3237) simply wraps this. The docstring examples (lines 3222-3229) confirm the (factor, multiplicity) format. Uncertainty: I did not inspect dup_gf_sqf_list or the exact ordering logic, but the reported behavior matches the documented contract, so no code change is warranted; the user's expectation of merging same-multiplicity factors is the inconsistency.

The W042 warning is emitted by Model._check_default_pk (django/db/models/base.py:1298-1320). Its condition is simply `cls._meta.pk.auto_created and not settings.is_overridden('DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD') and not cls._meta.app_config._is_default_auto_field_overridden`. It does not distinguish a PK that was auto-created on the model itself from one inherited/promoted from a parent, so any model whose `_meta.pk.auto_created` is True triggers the warning.

Where auto_created comes from: Options._prepare (django/db/models/options.py:271-287). For a model with no explicit pk and no parents, it creates `pk_class(verbose_name='ID', primary_key=True, auto_created=True)` (line 286). For a child model with parents, it promotes the first parent link and sets `field.primary_key = True` (lines 272-283) without clearing auto_created, so the inherited PK keeps auto_created=True from the ancestor's auto field. That is why models inheriting from a base like `Entity` (whose PK is an auto-created AutoField) still report W042 even though the user never asked for a new auto PK on the child.

So the report is consistent with a real bug/limitation in the 3.2 check: the check keys off `pk.auto_created` rather than whether the model itself defined the PK. The fix would be in _check_default_pk (e.g. also require the PK to be a local field / not inherited), not in _prepare. I could not read the W042 tests (tests/check_framework/test_model_checks.py read failed), so I cannot confirm whether a test already covers inherited PKs; that is the main uncertainty. The hint text and app-config override logic (django/apps/config.py:64-70) are unrelated to the false positive.
